tasks.registered_metrics_text:
a) Define the metric(s) to assess a property of an algorithm. These metrics should reflect the desired algorithm
properties described in assessment aim(s) (see above). State which metric(s) were used to compute the ranking(s) (if
any).
  • Example 1: Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC)
  • Example 2: Area under curve (AUC)
Customized score system with weighted of global and local metrics.
Global metrics include: Normalized root mean squared error (NRMSE), peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and
structural similarity index measurement (SSIM).
Local metrics will be calculated within delineated sphere volume of interest (VOI) of targeted organs (liver, kidney
and lung). Percentage error of clinical imaging parameters including SUVmean, SUVmax, total lesion metabolism


 Ultra-low Dose PET Imaging Challenge 2023

(TLM), as well as the most relevant radiomics features (GLRLM: High Gray Level Run Emphasis, GLSZM: Zone
Percentage, GLCM: Joint Average, First order: RootMeanSquared, First order: 90Percentile, First order: Median), as
well as local PSNR will be calculated between recovered images to the full-dose images.
More detailed description can be found on our website: https://ultra-low-dose-pet.grandchallenge.
org/Evaluation/


Local metrics will be calculated within delineated sphere volume of interest (VOI) of targeted organs as well as
lesions.

b) Justify why the metric(s) was/were chosen, preferably with reference to the biomedical application.

The global physical metrics are used to evaluate the general image quality of recovered imaging, which is standard
criteria in PET image denoising.
The local clinical imaging parameters and radiomics features are used to evaluate the recovery of detailed
information and texture.
tasks.registered_ranking_text:
a) Describe the method used to compute a performance rank for all submitted algorithms based on the generated
metric results on the test cases. Typically the text will describe how results obtained per case and metric are aggregated
to arrive at a final score/ranking.

Team rankings are computed using weighted scores from each evaluation metric. We will calculate measures using
python scripts. Evaluation code will be available together with training dataset so teams can test first.
Particularly, for each individual test subject, weights for different dose reduced factor (DRF) are 5%, 15%, 20%, 25%,
35%, 50% in terms of DRF=4,10,20,50,100, and real low-dose data. As for assessment metrics, 50% weight would be
applied to global metrics (40% for NRMSE, 40% for PSNR and 20% for SSIM), and 50% weight would be applied to
local metrics (40% for SUV parameters and 30% for TLM and PSNR, and the rest 30% will be evenly allocated to
radiomics parameters).


As for assessment metrics, 30% weight would be applied to global metrics (30% for NRMSE, 30% for PSNR and 40%
for SSIM), and 35% (Targeted organs) + 35% (Lesions) weight would be applied to local metrics (45% for SUV
parameters and 25% for TLM and PSNR, and the rest 30% will be evenly allocated to radiomics parameters).


More detailed description can be found on our website: https://ultra-low-dose-pet.grandchallenge.
org/Evaluation/

b) Describe the method(s) used to manage submissions with missing results on test cases.

If the submission doesn't include any of the test subject, they will not be evaluated.

c) Justify why the described ranking scheme(s) was/were used.

The importance of each metrics are different, for example, the global physical metrics would be given bigger
weights compared to local radionics features. Meanwhile, the difficulties and importance of the recovery from
different dose reduced low dose image are different, for example, the larger the reduction factor is, the larger
weight would be given to the score.


In regard to intra-group weights, we have determined that NRMSE and PSNR measure similar properties of global
image quality i.e., L2 distance. As such, we have allocated 40% to SSIM and 30% to each of NRMSE and PSNR. We


 Ultra-low Dose PET Imaging Challenge 2023

have also recognized that SUV related metrics, particularly SUVmax, hold greater clinical relevance than radiomic
features. Therefore, we have assigned more weight to SUV metrics.
With regards to inter-group weights, we have determined that local metrics of targeted organs and lesions are
more important than global metrics. Consequently, we have allocated 70% to local metrics and targeted organs
and lesions.

registered_task_submissions.protocol_description: Detailed submission instructions are provided on our website: https://ultra-low-dose-pet.grand-challenge.org/submission/ For successful participation and consideration for prizes, participants will be required to submit: · A short paper or abstract about your method · Algorithms scripts or link to your Github repository · Generated Full dose image, recovered from dose reduced images in Test dataset · Pre-registration via Email to Song Xue (song.xue@unibe.ch) by September 10th, 2023 to confirm a submission by the deadline. Submitted generated images should: · use the same file structure as test.zip · voxel value using the same unit as test.zip -- Bq/mL · all images are stored in compressed nifty file (.nii.gz) Submission should be directly sent to Song Xue (song.xue@unibe.ch) via Email.
